prose_updates.tldr: This is a statistical-inference paper about a causal ADRF under two blind nonidentical asymmetric replicates. Analytic cocycle identification and an explicit structural response-surface condition establish the causal identifying functional. The finite-dimensional, semi-infinite deterministic constrained-sieve band is uniformly honest, clipped to \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\), and has uniformly \(o(1)\) expected maximal width after Sobolev-modulus constraints are added. A parallel abstract exact-class band gives the same qualitative consistency conclusion. Neither construction proves the candidate \(r_n\) rate, and the fixed-nuisance Bernoulli lower modulus remains unresolved, so there is no matched honest-band rate.

project_justification.gap: Existing statistical results cover blind repeated-measurement density estimation, confidence bands under auxiliary-error, symmetric-error, or fixed-operator designs, and pointwise continuous-treatment inference. They do not provide a quantitative simultaneous ADRF band rate for blind nonidentical asymmetric replicate errors with open spectral zero sets. The remaining upper-side gap is an explicit modulus for the protected-cube marked analytic inverse, and the remaining lower-side gap is the fixed-nuisance Bernoulli packet needed for a sharp all-band converse.
project_justification.niche: The inferential niche is a nonlinear severe inverse problem: compact treatment support supplies entire transforms, one centered replicate fixes translation, the moment radius itself supplies a protected near-zero neighborhood, and the causal target is a stratum-weighted quotient. Sobolev moduli compactify both exact and finite-sieve signal sequences, converting qualitative channel identification into uniform consistency while keeping quantitative rate inversion separate.
project_justification.fill: The paper delivers two uniformly honest and uniformly consistent inference maps. The finite-dimensional, semi-infinite deterministic construction uses spline, frequency, truncation, and atomic dimensions; simultaneous probability-, marked-, and mass-channel radii; equicontinuous relaxed outer signal sieves; a joint feasible set; and measurable clipped ADRF extrema. Its expected maximal width is bounded by \(\widetilde\omega_n+2b_{\mu,n}+2B_Y|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}=o(1)\). No finite decision algorithm is claimed. In parallel, exact empirical-channel residuals are profiled over a compact projected nuisance class and yield a conceptual exact-class band. Both arguments are qualitative: no explicit \(O(r_n)\) upper or matching marked converse is claimed.

sampling_model.design: The data are an i.i.d. sample of marked blind two-replicate observations \(O_i=(Y_i,X_i,S_{i1},S_{i2})\).
sampling_model.units: Superpopulation units have finite-stratum \(X_i\), compact latent dose \(A_i\), and bounded potential-outcome schedules generated simultaneously as \(Y_i(a)=h(a,X_i,V_i)\) by a jointly measurable response surface, with \(V_i\perp A_i\mid X_i\); the stratum-specific causal means are continuous on \(I\).
sampling_model.treatment: The replicates satisfy \(S_{i1}=A_i+U_{i1}\) and \(S_{i2}=A_i+U_{i2}\). The errors are independent, need not be identically distributed or symmetric, may have open spectral zero sets, obey one fixed \(q_e>1\) moment radius, and use only \(E[U_2]=0\) to fix location. Their protected near-zero modulus is derived from the moment bound rather than imposed as a separate class restriction.
sampling_model.overlap: The target interval obeys \(f_x(a)\ge\kappa\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(a\in I\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The finite-dimensional, semi-infinite deterministic profiling construction uses relaxed order-\(d\) B-spline families for \(f_x,q_x\), intersected with deterministic Sobolev-modulus inequalities, finite atomic characteristic-function families for both errors, and \(p_x\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\) against simultaneous empirical probability- and marked-channel restrictions on \(\mathcal D_n\). The continuum inequalities are imposed exactly, so no finite decision algorithm is claimed. A second abstract construction profiles the same empirical radii over the exact compact projected class \(\mathscr K\).
sampling_model.tails: Outcomes are uniformly bounded by \(B_Y\), while each measurement error has a fixed \(q_e>1\) absolute-moment bound \(M_e\).

prose_updates.related_work: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy provide the unmarked probability-channel cocycle and compact-support density analysis that inform this paper. Their Theorem 1 assumes coordinate independence for the noise and condition H2 for the signal; compact support places the present probability signal inside H2 with \(\rho=1\). The present unmarked probability submodel is therefore contained in their normalized scalar signal-identification setting, but is stricter because it additionally fixes error moments and centers \(U_2\); their theorem also identifies error laws up to translation, whereas the present marked theorem claims only \(f_x,q_x\). Their rate and minimax theorems add second-moment and protected-frequency conditions and concern \(L^2\) density risk, so those rates do not imply an ADRF supremum-band rate. Gassiat, Le Corff, and Lehéricy supply the broader analytic-continuation principle for blind deconvolution. Huang and Zhang formulate the error-contaminated continuous-treatment ADRF and derive pointwise inference with a known everywhere-nonzero error transform. Kato and Sasaki (2018) develop deconvolution bands with an auxiliary error sample and a symmetric-error repeated-measurement route; Kato and Sasaki (2019) establish uniform bands under conventional spectral conditions. Kato, Sasaki, and Ura invert Kotlarski restrictions without completeness. Babii studies honest expected diameter for fixed linear inverse operators. Low supplies a testing-to-expected-length reduction only after a marked modulus is established. None supplies the missing quantitative marked inverse or the fixed-nuisance Bernoulli converse for the present blind quotient problem.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The model fixes compact dose support, bounded outcomes, Sobolev radii with \(\beta>1/2\), overlap, an error moment radius with \(q_e>1\), positive finite-stratum masses, and the structural causal response surface. It imposes no separate local spectral-modulus condition: \(|\phi_Q(t)|\ge1-|t|M_e^{1/q_e}\) supplies \(\nu_*=(2M_e^{1/q_e})^{-1}\) and \(c_*=1/2\). For all sufficiently large \(n\), the finite-dimensional, semi-infinite deterministic outer-sieve band is uniformly honest, clipped to width at most \(2B_Y\), and has uniformly \(o(1)\) expected maximal width. The exact-class band remains a parallel conceptual construction with the same qualitative conclusion. No \(O(r_n)\), minimax-matching, or rate-elbow claim is made; the fixed-nuisance marked-modulus open question remains unresolved.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The causal bridge, analytic-cocycle identification, simultaneous transform concentration, equicontinuous outer-sieve embedding, clipped uniform coverage, and qualitative finite-sieve target-diameter contraction are proved. Compactness shows \(\widetilde\omega_n\to0\), but supplies no numerical inverse modulus, so the finite-dimensional semi-infinite band has no established logarithmic rate despite uniform consistency. The sharp-rate program still requires a protected-cube quantitative inverse for both probability and signed marked channels. The fixed-nuisance Bernoulli outcome modulus remains the lower-side obstruction.
prose_updates.interpretation: The observed two-channel law identifies the continuous regression curve \(q_x/f_x\). Structural exogeneity first equates this curve with the stratum-specific causal mean almost everywhere in dose; positivity and continuity extend the equality to every target dose. The Sobolev modulus prevents increasingly oscillatory feasible splines and turns expanding-grid channel agreement into qualitative whole-curve contraction. The Melaku--Shi (2026) two-recall diet--mortality analysis motivates this design, but coverage applies to that application only insofar as its data-generating law satisfies the stated compact-support, overlap, structural-response, moment, and smoothness conditions.
